questions.prompt: In self-consistency, what should you vote on?

options.text: The full text of each response
The final answer extracted from each sampled reasoning path

questions.explanation: Different reasoning paths can reach the same answer with different wording. Extract the final answers and pick the most common one.

questions.prompt: Which statements about self-critique (generate, critique, revise) are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: It works best when the critique checks explicit criteria
It catches careless errors better than knowledge errors
Running steps as separate calls lets you log and inspect each one

questions.explanation: A model reviewing itself shares its blind spots, so self-critique can't guarantee facts. Explicit criteria and separate steps make it far more useful.

questions.prompt: The share of samples that produced the winning answer, used as a confidence signal, is the ____ rate.
questions.explanation: High agreement suggests a reliable answer; split votes suggest routing the question to a human, a tool, or a stronger check.

questions.prompt: A model without search is asked to explain a topic and cite sources with links. What's the main risk?

options.text: The links will all be too old
It may produce plausible but fabricated citations
It will refuse every request with links

questions.explanation: Without retrieval, citations are generated text like anything else. Provide sources or use search, and check every link.

questions.prompt: Order these verification methods from strongest to weakest, as the lesson ranks them (excluding human review).
questions.explanation: Deterministic checks can't be talked into a wrong answer; sources come next; independent review beats self-critique, which shares the model's blind spots.

questions.prompt: Match each technique to what it gives you.

pairs.right: A voted answer plus an agreement signal
A checklist of claims to verify

questions.explanation: Each technique adds a different kind of reliability: voting, transparency, a verification checklist, or iterative improvement.
